explanation: Repeat 32 times: multiply the result by two, append n modulo two, then replace n by floor(n/2). Number represents every intermediate integer exactly because all are at most 2^32-1.
timeComplexity: O(32), constant time for the fixed-width input. The loop executes exactly 32 fixed-cost rounds.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Only the result, remaining input, and loop count are retained.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: After i rounds, result is the reversal of the lowest i original bits. Multiplication by two opens a low-bit position and n modulo two supplies the next original bit. Dividing n by two discards that bit. Exactly 32 rounds include leading zeros and preserve the unsigned result.
walkthrough: For n=3, original bits 0 and 1 are set. Reversing 32 positions moves them to bits 31 and 30, giving 0xC0000000, or unsigned value 3221225472. Return that value in a long.
edgeCases: Exactly 32 bits are reversed, not all 64 bits of the carrier type.
The result is nonnegative in the range 0..2^32-1.
